claim: EPP peer discovery is a separate mechanism from leader election, used only for active-active cross-replica state sync (e.g. future prefix-cache metadata exchange).
quoted_support: EPP replicas operating in an active-active topology need to know about each other so a future cross-replica syncer can exchange state (e.g. prefix-cache metadata) between them.

claim: Peer discovery is configured via a generic pluginRef, not a hardwired Kubernetes mechanism, and is disabled by default.
stance_target: existence of a Kubernetes-independent peer-discovery path
quoted_support: It is configured via dataLayer.discovery.peers.pluginRef in the EndpointPickerConfig. Implementations are registered in the plugin registry and selected by name. When omitted, peer discovery is disabled and no peer set is maintained.

claim: No built-in peer-discovery plugin implementation (kubernetes, file, or static) is named in the doc; the only example given is a custom hand-written plugin.
stance_target: whether a file/static peer-discovery plugin exists as an alternative to a kubernetes one
scope_conditions: llm-d-router repo, docs/peer-discovery.md as of the fetched commit
quoted_support: Implement fwkdl.PeerDiscovery and register the factory with the plugin registry. A runnable example of this pattern is in the test suite... package myplugin ... const PluginType = "my-peer-discovery"

claim: PeerStore is deliberately architecturally separated from Datastore (endpoint store) to avoid coupling the peer-tracking subsystem to the endpoint/scheduling subsystem.
quoted_support: PeerStore and Datastore share the same Upsert/Delete/notifier shape, but they serve different consumers and have different lifecycles... Keeping them separate avoids coupling unrelated subsystems.

claim: The PeerNotifier interface is not goroutine-safe and requires strict single-goroutine sequential ordering of Upsert/Delete calls, but the doc specifies no cross-replica reconciliation or consistency guarantee for divergent peer-discovery sources (e.g. file-based).
stance_target: endpoint/peer datastore consistency across active-active replicas using file/custom discovery
quoted_support: PeerNotifier is not goroutine-safe. All Upsert and Delete calls must be made sequentially from a single goroutine so that an Upsert followed by a Delete for the same peer is applied in that order.
